explicit_behavior_differences: Serial loop publishes each successful prefix entry before a later failure. Batch workers use private empty dicts; owner guards publish only after every file result and staged owner/duplicate conflict check succeeds. Any failure leaves owner guards unchanged.

All descriptors are prevalidated before submission. A malformed later descriptor may become the first error rather than an earlier byte failure. With valid descriptors, results are observed in input order, but owner conflicts are checked only after file results, so multiple-fault first-error precedence can still differ.

Physical open/read completion order is concurrent, not serial. A failure can cause more files to be read than the serial failing prefix. Executor shutdown joins submitted work before returning/raising; it does not promise cancellation of queued tasks.

The helper materializes items and submits all futures: four bounds active workers, not queued bookkeeping. Approximately four 1 MiB streaming buffers plus O(18620) items/futures/results/staged guards require actual RSS/resource qualification.
